newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks reverse gains on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks reverse gains on profit-taking.

text.p: The Mexican bourse reversed its opening gains at mid-session on Thursday and took a break from its recent upward charge after profit-takers finally stepped in, analysts and traders said.
"This is quite normal and healthy. Several technical indicators were overvalued, so profit-taking is just releasing pressure from prices because they had gained very quickly," an equity analyst said.
The leading IPC share index .MXX was down 13.71 points, or 0.33 percent, at 4,107.85.
"Then there's Telmex, which has turned around," the analyst added.
The telecomms stock had fallen two centavos to 18.58 pesos in Mexico, while its ADRs had shed their early increase to stand unchanged at 46-7/8 on Wall Street.
Telmex accounted for some 10 percent of all shares traded. Nonetheless, dealers noted that one single cross trade accounted for 9.3 million shares out of a light total of 68.5 million traded .Tv.MX.
On the broad market, of 98 stocks traded, sliders outpaced gainers by 64 to 22.
